```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B names a specific customer, a Wisconsin public adjuster and an affiliated roofing contractor. A names no customer ('varies by idea') and admits its own description is unconfirmed ('one-line description to confirm'). A 90-day path to a paying customer is far more plausible when a candidate buyer is already identified.",
    "B's willingness to pay is shown by several direct competitors with sourced pricing selling to the same buyer: ClaimWizard at $99–$250/mo, claimOS at $199/mo plus $99/user, Claim Titan from $82.50/user, and AdjustCRM at $65/user. A's named direct competitors are all free and pre-revenue. Its only priced comparable, CoFoundersLab at $29/mo, is in an adjacent category and carries a class-action billing complaint.",
    "B's demand evidence comes from operators describing the pain: a Pipedrive case study quoting a PA ops director on manual processes, and a small PA on Reddit asking for a simple claims CRM. A's demand evidence is a single Reddit thread that also contains a direct rebuttal to the premise, namely that vibe coding removes the need for an 'ideas guy'.",
    "B's core build, intake plus document extraction, is a bounded AI task that a solo operator with agents can scope. A's product is undefined, so its scope cannot be judged.",
    "B has serious risks: a 188-licensee in-state market, five or more entrenched competitors, scope creep into full claim-lifecycle management, and Wisconsin data-security and breach-notification obligations. These mainly limit scale and add compliance work. They do not block landing one paying first customer. A's risks go to whether any demand exists at all: a saturated field of no-traction clones and AI tools eroding the core need."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's acquisition-cost estimate ($100–200 per paying customer via niche communities) is the thinnest load-bearing claim. The brief itself flags its source, launchedly.app, as an unverified vendor blog. No figure in the brief ties it to this product, and with no product or payer defined, any CAC figure is unsupported. Its payer anchor is also weak: it rests entirely on CoFoundersLab, which sits in an adjacent category and carries a billing class-action.",
  "confidence_note": "High confidence that B is the better first bet. The briefs separate clearly: B has an identified customer, direct competitors with sourced pricing, and specific operator pain. A has an unresolved concept, free pre-revenue competitors, and a community rebuttal of its premise. Confidence would drop if B's 'existing customer' commitment proves informal. The brief lists that as an open question, and the claim that the customer pair already exists is not independently evidenced. Confidence would also drop if Wisconsin data-security compliance cannot be met within the timeline."
}
```
